## Creating

Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of each section, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a story there, open, its title focused, in the mode last picked for a story. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as its prompt.
A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), to break it into stories, each with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or rejected, and none reaches the Backlog until it is accepted. An Ask answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to backlog", which adds the card's prompt as a story in its mode.

## Sprint
## Drafting

Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than the Backlog's heading.

## Proposals

The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, able to read the project and change nothing, and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says; a block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so.
Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at its top, "New story" in the theme's accent or "Add to" and the story's title in Spec's or the story's own mode's colour; its title, its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.
Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens it.
Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

## Research

The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.
Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

## Paused

Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, each story's Send, the ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled, their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.
The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review", names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends; nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.
The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed or approved.

## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter sends the focused story, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.

Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.
Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

## Paused

Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, each story's Send, the ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled, their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.
The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review", names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends; nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.
The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed or approved.

## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter sends the focused story, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.

## Suggested Prompts

An answer can hand back a prompt for the user to send, as a fenced code block whose info string is `suspense-prompt`, followed by a space and the mode it is meant for, `code`, `chain`, `spec`, `ask`, or `freeform`, as the [PromptModes](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes) names them, and holding the prompt's text, as the card format of the [ModeSystemPrompts](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) tells the harness. Such a block is never shown as a code block. It is shown in the answer, where it stands among the reply's markdown, as a prompt card: a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted the mode's colour, with corners rounded 6 pixels, across the answer's full width. Along its top runs a small header, the mode's icon and name in the mode's colour, as "Code prompt", and beneath it the prompt's text as it was written, wrapped, in the body's text colour, not rendered as markdown.
A card starts collapsed, its text cut to its first line, cut off with an ellipsis, and a chevron at the right of its header. Clicking the header or the chevron expands it to show the whole prompt, the chevron turning down, and clicking again collapses it; its buttons work either way, sending or copying the whole prompt. Each card stays as it was left for as long as the application runs, and expanding or collapsing one never scrolls the pane. Along its bottom, at its right, is a row of small buttons, 4 pixels apart, wrapping onto another line where the card is too

### Narrow

Copy, with a copy icon, which puts the prompt's text on the

clipboard; Edit, with a pencil icon, as below; "Add to sprint", with a list icon, which adds the prompt as a story in the card's mode to the Planning's Next sprint and reads "Added" with a check after; and then "Send to Code", "Send to Chain", and "Send to Spec", in that order, each with an arrow icon and in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModes](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes) colours them. The send button for the card's own mode, where it is one of those three, is filled in its colour, and the others are ghost buttons in theirs, so the one the answer meant stands out while every task mode is a click away. A card for `ask` or `freeform` has, before the three, "Ask" or "Send to Freeform", filled in that mode's colour, the three after it as ghosts.
Each send button sends the prompt's text at once, in its mode, as though it had been written in the [ChatInput](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input) on that tab and sent, as the [PromptSending](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says, the Chain button sending it as a Chain prompt: a task is compiled anew, building the spec first, and queues while its lane is busy, and a question runs at once. It is sent with the Slice toggle as it stands, with nothing attached, and what is being written in the chat input, and attached to it, is left alone. The button then reads "Sent to Code", "Sent to Chain", "Sent to Spec", "Asked", or "Sent to Freeform", with a check, and keeps reading so: it never times out or resets, and it is disabled for good, so the prompt is never sent twice from it, however long after, and across restarts, kept with the question's record. The card's other send buttons stay as they were, so the prompt can still be sent to another mode, each once. The tooltip of each says what it does, as "Send this prompt as a Code task".
Edit puts the prompt's text in the chat input's text input instead, and selects the card's mode's tab, Chain for Code and Spec selected together where the mode is `chain`, giving the input keyboard focus with the cursor at the end of the text. It never sends anything: the user reads, edits, and sends it as any prompt. Where the input already holds text, that text is set aside first as the chat input sets aside a prompt for editing a queued one, and comes back once the prompt from the card is sent or cleared, so nothing typed is lost. What is attached to the prompt being written stays attached. The button reads "Edited", with a check, for 2 seconds after.
A block whose mode is missing or isn't one of those five is still a prompt card, headed "Prompt", in Ask's colour, with all three send buttons as ghosts, and Edit selects Chain, the tab the chat input starts on. While a block is still streaming in, its card is shown with what has come so far and its buttons disabled until the block closes. A block never closed by the end of a finished answer is a card all the same, holding what came. An answer may hold any number of cards, each in its place.

The agent now only proposes during planning. Nothing reaches the plan until you accept it. The planning tests (including five new ones), the sprint, ribbon, card, answer-block and baked-prompt tests pass in a scratch copy; the one failure there is the fluency test, because the copy has a stand-in fluency file. I haven't tried it in the running app.

**What changed:**
- **Read-only drafting:** drafting now runs as a Question run, which can read the project but change nothing and gets no access to `.suspense`. Its live line shows what the agent is doing ("Reading …", "Searching for …"), and Stop now actually ends the run.
- **Proposals:** `planning.pi` now asks for `suspense-story` blocks, each with a title, mode, target (`new` or a story's id) and prompt. The agent is shown the stories it can add to.
- **Proposal cards:** each proposal is a card showing "New story" or "Add to <story>", with Accept, Edit and Reject.
  - Edit changes the title, prompt, mode or target in place.
  - Reject leaves an Undo for 5 seconds.
  - "Accept all" and "Reject all" sit at the panel's foot, and the panel closes once nothing is left to decide.
  - Proposals are saved in `order.json` until decided.
  - A, E and R work on the focused card.
- **Accepting a new story:** it goes to the end of the Backlog with a "From agent" sparkle until first opened.
- **Accepting an addition:** it becomes a new step at the end of the named story. The story is marked "Updated by agent" and the step is highlighted the next time you open it.
  - If the story has been deleted or already sent, nothing is added. The card stays, switched to "New story", and says why.
- **Ask agent:** on a story's menu and in the open story, it drafts about that story. The panel opens beneath it and asks "What does this story need?".
- **Ask answers:** a `suspense-story` block in an answer becomes a card with Accept, Edit and Reject.

**Where I followed the spec over the chain's summary, or fell short:**
- **Additions are steps:** the spec step's summary said an addition is appended to the story's prompt as a paragraph. The spec itself says it becomes a new step, so I followed the spec.
- **Steps outside Chain stories aren't sent:** steps only run after the story when the story's mode is Chain, because that uses the app's existing chain-step mechanism. For Code, Spec, Ask and Freeform stories, steps are saved and shown but not sent. The spec's full Steps section (adding, reordering and sending steps for any story) isn't built.
- **Edit on an Ask card moves it to Planning:** it moves the proposal into Planning's panel to edit there, rather than editing inside the answer.
- **"Add to sprint":** the Ask prompt card's "Add to backlog" is now "Add to sprint" and adds to Next sprint. The current Ask spec says so, though this chain's prompt didn't ask for it.
- **Not built:** the spec's new Research and Paused sections weren't among this chain's anchors.
